source_caption:
One of the most unforgettable scenes in 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐒𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐞 (𝟐𝟎𝟏𝟕) is the infamous gala dinner sequence, where performance artist Oleg, played by motion-capture legend Terry Notary, slowly transforms an elegant black-tie event into absolute chaos.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
What makes the scene even more fascinating is that many of the guests Oleg intimidates weren’t actors. They were drawn from the real Swedish art elite, including some of the country’s wealthiest collectors and museum patrons. Terry Notary didn’t even know this until filming was almost over. “They were so into it,” he later recalled. Rather than targeting the volunteers who wanted to interact with him, he deliberately chose the people who looked the most uncomfortable, creating reactions that feel startlingly authentic.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Director Ruben Östlund said the sequence was designed as an experiment in human behavior:⁣⁣
⁣⁣
“These people that in the beginning were sitting in tuxedos and eating their nice, fancy dinner, I wanted them to be uncivilized animals in the end. I think that the most uncivilized thing about our time is the collective rage against individuals that are acting uncivilized. Isn’t that the scary thing about us?”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
The scene is also a study of the bystander effect. Everyone waits for someone else to intervene while Oleg’s behavior grows increasingly violent. As fear spreads through the room, the sophisticated guests become frozen, more concerned with not becoming the next target than with helping anyone else. Östlund has said that, like herd animals, humans often become paralyzed when confronted with unexpected danger.

source_details.title: The Square
source_details.synopsis: The Square is a 2017 satirical black comedy film written and directed by Ruben Östlund. The film stars Claes Bang, Elisabeth Moss, Dominic West and Terry Notary. A Swedish production with co-production support from Germany, France and Denmark, it was shot in Gothenburg, Stockholm and Berlin. The story was partly inspired by an installation Östlund and producer Kalle Boman had made. Östlund was also inspired by a notorious incident involving Oleg Kulik and cast Notary in a parody, drawing on Notary's experience imitating apes.
